newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lebed tells German TV that Yeltsin drinking again.
newsitem.headline: Lebed tells German TV that Yeltsin drinking again.

text.p: Former Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said in a television interview released on Friday that President Boris Yeltsin had started drinking alcohol against doctors' orders.
According to the text of the interview to be broadcast on Sunday by the German network ZDF, Lebed said he had sources close to Yeltsin who told him that the president was drinking.
"He has begun to drink," said Lebed, sacked by Yeltsin as security chief in October. "But he is not permitted to drink."
In Moscow, a Kremlin spokesman, asked about Lebed's remarks, said: "Does it matter when somebody says something somewhere. We do not comment on such things."
Yeltsin, who underwent quintuple bypass heart surgery in November, was always known as a man who enjoyed his vodka and persistent rumours suggested that he had a drinking problem.
Yeltsin's doctors have never said that he would be banned from alcohol after his operation, although U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said he would have to cut back on his drinking.
But DeBakey, a consultant during the surgery, said the Russian leader was not an alcholic. He said he had examined his liver and it was "perfectly normal."
Yeltsin missed several meetings during his presidency, including one with half the Irish government, when foreign news media speculated that he was ill or drunk. The Kremlin always denied it.

Asked by the ZDF interviewer how he knew that Yeltsin was drinking again, Lebed, who was brought into the government after winning 15 percent of the vote in the first round of this year's presidential election, said he would not identify his sources.

Asked when he expected to return to the Kremlin, he said: "I will always be only in the Kremlin. Today we have the reason that will happen before the year 2000 because after the successful operation, after the colossal work that the doctors performed, the last hopes have been extinguished.
"He (Yeltsin) began to drink. But he is not permitted to drink."
